3	# The container, the transcripts, and recovery
4	
5	A session in this setup is a conversation in a remote container that can be
6	reclaimed or corrupted at any time, and is re-provisioned by cloning a branch.
7	Three things therefore have to be true at all times: the work is pushed, the
8	transcript is pushed, and the branch the infrastructure clones is current.
9	
10	## What is where
11	
12	| thing | where | note |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| the work | `main`, and the container's infrastructure branch | both kept at the same commit, see *The branch trap* |
15	| session transcripts | orphan branches `transcripts` and `transcripts-blinded` | no shared history with `main`; large blobs live only there |
16	| live transcripts on disk | `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/` | `<session>.jsonl`, plus per-session directories |
17	| the snapshot scripts | `<worktree>/scripts/` on each orphan branch — **these are the copies that run** | reference copy in `explorations/coordinator/transcript-backup/` |
18	| the backup's log and state | `<worktree>/.backup.log`, `.backup.state`, `.backup.lock`, `.backup.pending` | never committed (the branch's `.gitignore`: `/.backup.*`) |
19	
20	Two orphan branches exist because the blinded microGPT runs were a controlled
21	experiment: neither run's container was to hold the other's transcripts.
22	`transcripts` holds the coordinating sessions, `transcripts-blinded` the
23	blinded-run container's. Keep them apart; join them at analysis time, which
24	costs nothing — see *Reading another session's transcript*.
25	
26	## How the snapshot works
27	
28	A `Stop` hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` runs `<worktree>/scripts/backup.sh`
29	at the end of every assistant turn. Since `transcripts-blinded@974d9be7`
30	(2026-09-29) the hook returns at once: it records a request
31	(`.backup.pending`) and, unless a runner already holds the lock
32	(`.backup.lock`, taken with `flock`), starts `backup.sh --run` detached in the
33	background, and exits 0. The runner makes one pass per request until none is
34	left. `backup_transcripts.py` copies the live JSONL into the worktree with two
35	policy redactions (deck page images, HANDOVER.md contents); the runner then
36	commits `projects/`, pushes whenever the branch is ahead of its upstream
37	(retrying after 2, 4, 8 and 16 s), and packs loose objects. Each pass writes
38	one line to `<worktree>/.backup.log`, the last 200 kept: its time, the
39	copier's time and exit code, the commit, how far the branch was ahead, and the
40	push's result. The copier is incremental: `.backup.state` records each
41	source's size and modification time and the files written for it, and a
42	source whose record and snapshot files still match is skipped without being
43	read. A pass takes about 10 s (8.5 to 11.7 s between 17:50 and 18:00 UTC on
44	2026-09-29, the copier about 1 s of it). These properties matter:
45	
46	- **It fires on the main session's Stop, not on any agent's completion.** A
47	  session that sits inside one long turn is not being backed up, however much
48	  work its agents are doing. This is the single largest gap in the design.
49	- **It swallows every error and never holds up the session**, so a failing
50	  push is silent. Read the `push=` field of the last line of `.backup.log`, or
51	  `git -C <worktree> status -sb`.
52	- **It snapshots every session in the container**, not just the current one.
53	- **A container that dies within about 10 s of a turn ending loses that turn's
54	  snapshot**: the pass runs after the hook has returned, and takes that long.
55	- **Only `index.lock` is cleaned automatically.** A git process killed
56	  mid-command leaves its lock behind. The runner removes an `index.lock` at
57	  least 10 s old that no process has open, and waits out a younger one. A
58	  stale lock on the branch's ref, `/home/user/fortress/.git/refs/heads/transcripts-blinded.lock`
59	  (the worktree shares the main repository's refs), is not cleaned: every
60	  later commit fails on it, `commit=failed` in the log, until it is removed by
61	  hand, after checking that no git process is running.
62	- A `SessionStart` hook with matcher `compact` (2026-09-27, on Pavol's yes) injects, after every compaction, the instruction to boot by `coordinator/README.md` before anything else. It is in the tracked `.claude/settings.json` and in `~/.claude/settings.json`; a fresh container copies the second from the first.
63	- The platform's own Stop hook, `~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh`, posts reminders about uncommitted or unpushed work after a turn. It comes from the launcher: the session's process is started with `--settings /root/.claude/launcher-settings.json`, whose `Stop` hook runs that script, and the script is rewritten at every process start. At Pavol's request on 2026-09-29 it was replaced by a no-op that reads its input and exits 0; the original is kept in the session scratchpad, `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/stop-hook-git-check.sh.orig`. It returns at each restart of the process, and turning it off again is Pavol's to do, in manual mode: the auto-mode permission check refused scheduling it. The coordinator's push loop covers what it protected: `autopush.sh` in the same scratchpad, every 4 minutes, pushes `main` and the container branch when every unpushed commit touches only `explorations/`, and otherwise pushes `main` to `wip/main-backup` only, so that a container reset loses nothing and `main` stays gated; it is started again after a process restart. While the hook is back, its reminders are advisory, declined without a word while held or gated changes exist, and never mentioned to Pavol.
64	
65	## Re-arming it in a fresh container
66	
67	```sh
68	git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded transcripts-blinded
69	# then register the Stop hook in ~/.claude/settings.json:
70	#   {"hooks":{"Stop":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command",
71	#     "command":"/home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/scripts/backup.sh"}]}]}}
72	/home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/scripts/backup.sh --run   # one pass, in the foreground
73	tail -1 /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/.backup.log       # verify
74	```
75	
76	The verify step: the log's last line reads `copier_rc=0` and either
77	`commit=<hash>` with `push=ok`, or, when nothing changed since the last pass,
78	`commit=none ahead=0 push=none`; `git -C <worktree> status -sb` shows the
79	branch not ahead of its upstream. Run by hand, `--run` waits for any runner at
80	work and then makes a pass. The hook's own form, without `--run`, returns at
81	once, and its pass shows in the log about 10 s later.
82	
83	`explorations/experiment/setup.sh` does this for the blinded lineage. Substitute
84	`transcripts` for the coordinating lineage, whose `scripts/` are still those of
85	2026-09-17: copy the reference copies in first. The script that runs is the one in
86	the worktree, on the branch — if you edit the reference copy under
87	`explorations/`, nothing changes until it is copied into the worktree.

89	## Three traps, each of which has cost us work
90	
91	**The workflow-transcript glob.** Agents launched by the `Workflow` tool do not
92	write where `Agent`-tool subagents do. Their transcripts, the run journal and
93	the persisted scripts live at
94	
95	```
96	projects/<proj>/<session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-*.jsonl, journal.jsonl, *.meta.json
97	projects/<proj>/<session>/workflows/scripts/<name>-<run>.js
98	```
99	
100	one level below the `subagents/*.jsonl` glob that the script used until
101	2026-09-18. Four workflow agents' transcripts — about 798k tokens — were
102	therefore never captured. Fixed; the fixture test in the commit message of
103	`transcripts-blinded@264d19c8` states what was verified.
104	
105	**The 100 MiB blob limit.** A snapshot rewrites the whole JSONL, so a long
106	session's transcript grows past GitHub's per-blob ceiling and the push fails —
107	silently, per above. A transcript over 64 MiB is now written as
108	`<session>.jsonl.parts/NNN.jsonl`, cut at line boundaries so that appends leave
109	every earlier part byte-identical. Rejoin with `cat <session>.jsonl.parts/*.jsonl`.
110	
111	**The loose-object pile.** The container's clone ships `gc.auto=0`, and each
112	snapshot writes whole files with no delta, so the object store grows by tens of
113	megabytes per commit: 21.3 GiB of loose objects by 2026-09-17, which packed down
114	to 609 MB. `backup.sh` now ends with `git -c gc.auto=1000 gc --auto`, run with
115	the runner's lock closed: until 2026-09-29 the detached `git gc` inherited the
116	lock and held it for as long as it ran, and every snapshot requested meanwhile
117	was silently skipped. Unrelated
118	but same symptom: the Rats! temp directories in `FACTS.md` § The container.
119	
120	**Worktree state that is never committed.** The first repair batch forbade its
121	workers to commit, so that the gather could compose one clean commit per rung;
122	when the container died every worktree was dirty and four agents' work went
123	with it. The transcript backup does not cover this: it copies JSONL, not trees,
124	and it fires only at the main session's Stop. The fix is in the workflow design
125	(`batched-climb-plan.md` §3, revised 2026-09-18): each worker's worktree is on
126	its own `wip/<slug>` branch, pushed at every milestone, and the gather composes
127	from the branch's net change instead of the dirty tree. Two rules follow for
128	any long run: nothing that takes hours lives only on disk, and the coordinator
129	takes a turn every 45 minutes, a series of `send_later` check-ins armed
130	together (`FACTS.md` § The container), so that the Stop hook fires and the
131	agents' transcripts are snapshotted while they run, and so that the session
132	stays cached, ready to launch the next batch (Pavol, 2026-09-26 23:37 UTC,
133	`POSITIONS-history.md`).
134	
135	## Setting up a batch's worktrees
136	
137	Since 2026-09-30 a climb batch's rung worker makes its own worktree, by the command in the batch script's shared prefix ("Your worktree"), and the coordinator makes none at the launch (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Shared prefix"). What follows is how the first batches were set up, and how a worktree is made by hand.
138	
139	The workflow script cannot touch the filesystem before its first agent runs, so
140	the coordinator creates the worktrees and pushes the empty branches first, from
141	the commit `main` is at, which is then the script's `args.base`:
142	
143	```sh
144	cd /home/user/fortress && BASE=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
145	for r in r1-atomic-static r2-literal-wrap; do
146	  git worktree add -b wip/repair-$r /home/user/fortress-${r%%-*} main
147	  cp -a ProjectFortress/build /home/user/fortress-${r%%-*}/ProjectFortress/   # javac incremental; scalac rebuilds anyway
148	  mkdir -p /home/user/fortress-${r%%-*}/tmp
149	  git push -u origin wip/repair-$r
150	done
151	```
152	
153	Copy the build, never symlink it: a symlinked build makes `ProjectProperties`
154	resolve every cache path to the main tree (`batched-climb-plan.md` §4). After
155	the batch lands, the commit stage removes the worktrees and local branches; the
156	remote `wip/` branches are deleted in the GitHub UI.
157	
158	## The branch trap
159	
160	The infrastructure clones the branch the session was created from. If work
161	proceeds on `main` while that branch is left behind, a re-provision lands on a
162	stale tree — or fails outright if the branch was renamed or deleted, which is
163	what ended the 2026-09-17 session: *"The requested branch or commit was not
164	found in the repository."* Keep the container's own branch fast-forwarded to
165	`main` whenever `main` moves.
166	
167	## Reading another session's transcript
168	
169	The orphan branches are in the same repository, so any session can read any
170	other's without switching or re-cloning:
171	
172	```sh
173	git fetch origin transcripts
174	git show origin/transcripts:projects/-home-user-fortress/<session>.jsonl.parts/000.jsonl | head
175	git grep -l 'some string' origin/transcripts -- 'projects/*'
176	```
177	
178	That is enough for targeted extraction. For sustained searching, materialise it
179	— `git worktree add /home/user/fortress-transcripts transcripts` — which costs a
180	second on-disk copy (296 MB on 2026-09-18) and does not affect where the hook
181	writes.
182	
183	## Recovering a session whose container died
184	
185	1. **Establish what was pushed.** `git rev-list --left-right --count <branch>...origin/main`.
186	   Work committed before the last push is safe; nothing else in the container is.
187	2. **Find the transcript's last record**, which bounds everything recoverable:
188	   the tail of the last `.parts/` file, against the last snapshot commit's time.
189	3. **Look for uncommitted edits in the tail** — mutating `Edit`/`Write`/`Bash`
190	   tool calls after the last push. Replay them by hand if any.
191	4. **Recover workflow scripts and briefs from the transcript.** A `Workflow`
192	   `tool_use` record carries its whole script; that is how the repair batch's
193	   30,751-character script was recovered on 2026-09-18.
194	5. **Do not expect to resume a workflow run.** `resumeFromRunId` is
195	   same-session-only and its cached agent results live in the dead session's
196	   run state. A run designed to be extended by a later resume cannot be
197	   finished from a new session — write the whole pipeline into one script
198	   instead.
199	6. **Write the handover before continuing**, from the transcript tail rather
200	   than from memory, and record the switch in `FACTS.md`.
201	
202	## The 2026-09-17 incident
203	
204	The coordinating session (`bdff267d-…`, on `transcripts`) launched the
205	`fortress-repair-batch` workflow at 19:26 and never reached another Stop. Its
206	last record is 20:31:14; the snapshot six seconds later is the last one. It was
207	still alive at about 21:07 — background tasks started then — and when it froze
208	is not knowable from the record. Its container could not be re-provisioned
209	because the branch it was created from was no longer found.

211	Lost: the four workflow agents (`rung:R1`, `rung:R2`, `skeptic:R1`,
212	`skeptic:R2`, ~798k tokens), their isolated worktrees, and the 13 hours after
213	the last snapshot. Not lost: everything committed through `2ab1d6d8`, the
214	workflow script, `REPAIR-BATCH.md` — written the same afternoon *"for a session
215	that was not present"*, which is why the batch remains runnable — and the
216	conversation through 20:31.
217	
218	Recovery was carried out in the blinded run's container, which already had the
219	checkout and the toolchain: fast-forward to `main`, fix the backup, materialise
220	the other lineage's transcripts, then re-run the batch from its recorded brief.
221	
222	## The 2026-09-19 interrupt
223	
224	A Workflow run lives inside the coordinating session's turn structure even though
225	it is reported as a background task: when Pavol interrupted the session's turn at
226	07:46:42 UTC, eleven seconds after a scheduled check-in had started it, both rung
227	agents of climb batch 1 stopped at that second and the harness forgot the task
228	(`TaskGet` returned not found). An `Agent`-tool worker launched afterwards was
229	unaffected. Recovery was the same as after the VM restart: the `wip/` branches
230	and the worktrees held everything pushed and everything on disk, and the batch
231	was relaunched from the same base with the same command. Two consequences: a
232	check-in that fires during a batch should be left to finish its turn, and,
233	since no agent had finished, there was nothing for a resume to keep. When one
234	has, the run is resumed with the same script text and `resumeFromRunId`, as
235	batch 6b was on 2026-09-27 (`FACTS.md`, "A restart of the session's own
236	process"; `resume-rule-archaeology.md`).
237	
238	A compaction is not an interrupt. The eight-rung climb of 2026-09-17 (run
239	`wf_73833dfb-d25`) ran through two manual `/compact` commands, at 10:47 and 14:25
240	UTC, both issued between turns, and completed at 14:39 with all eight rungs;
241	the evidence is the session's archived transcript (`bdff267d`, parts file
242	`001.jsonl`: the compact boundaries, the first post-compaction turn declining to
243	commit "the running workflow's rung 5", and the completion notification). So
244	while a batch runs: compact freely between turns; do not send while a turn is
245	in flight.
246	
247	*Corrected 2026-09-26:* the interrupt is not a message. What stops a turn, and
248	every background agent with it, Workflow agents and background `Agent`-tool
249	workers alike (two workers at 2026-09-22 07:18:51, one at 2026-09-25 22:31:59), is
250	the interrupt the transcript records as "[Request interrupted by user]"; on
251	2026-09-26 at 12:07:47 it was very likely the iOS stop button. A message sent
252	while a turn is in flight is queued, delivered inside the turn or as the next
253	turn, and in eleven cases from 09-19 to 09-26 it cut no turn and killed no run. So
254	while a batch runs: send whenever; compact between turns; do not press stop in any
255	turn, not only a check-in.
256	
257	## The 2026-09-18 restart
258	
259	The repair batch's re-run was launched at 22:57 UTC (run `wf_9777a563-c5e`,
260	session `fe616d40-…`). At about 23:22, 25 minutes in, the VM was restarted:
261	the two agents' last records are 23:22:20 and 23:22:23, a test's output file
262	was still being written at 23:22:29, and `uptime` read 0 minutes at 23:23:29
263	on a kernel whose build string had changed (fc-v33 to fc-v37). One JVM was
264	running across both worktrees at that moment, on 16 GB with no swap, so the
265	load was not the cause; a platform restart is the only reading the record
266	supports.
267	
268	What it cost: the two rung agents' working context, 25 minutes of two workers.
269	What it did not cost: the disk survived, so the worktrees, their uncommitted
270	edits, their `tmp/` logs and the agents' transcripts were all there afterwards
271	and the transcripts were snapshotted at the next Stop; and the `wip/` branches
272	held every milestone pushed before the restart — R1's two failing tests with
273	their recorded failure (23:12) and its fix with the recorded pass (23:21), R2's
274	failing test with its recorded failure (23:12). The batch was relaunched at
275	23:28 (run `wf_aabc0cb2-d31`) from the same base, and the shared prefix gained
276	a clause telling a worker whose branch already carries commits to read them
277	and continue, verifying rather than redoing. The relaunched batch landed at 03:22, so the
278	restart cost 25 minutes of two workers and nothing else.
279	
280	Two properties of the harness, learned here: a `Workflow` run does not survive
281	a VM restart even when the session does — its agents are gone, the harness
282	lists them as stopped, and `resumeFromRunId` holds nothing for an agent that
283	never finished, so the answer was a relaunch (on 2026-09-27 a resume in the same
284	session did recover the agents that had finished: `FACTS.md`, "A restart of the
285	session's own process"); and a `send_later` reminder is
286	server-side and does survive, so it is deleted or re-armed to fit the relaunch.

1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
     3	#
     4	# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
     5	# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
     6	# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
     7	#
     8	#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll`, the
     9	#                    restore of default_repository/caches/global.map and the library-order recompile
    10	#                    (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have run, and nothing since.
    11	#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
    12	#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
    13	#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
    14	#                    <start-point> instead. Old-against-new runs need no copy of the base: tools/old-fortress.sh
    15	#                    runs the base build itself with a private caches folder.
    16	#
    17	# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
    18	# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
    19	# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
    20	# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
    21	# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
    22	# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); and makes the
    23	# new worktree the base's replica in its file dates too. The copies keep the base's dates (cp -a), every
    24	# tracked file whose content is the base's takes the base file's date, and every tracked file that differs
    25	# from B, committed or not, is stamped later than everything copied. Dates decide three things. The
    26	# repository uses a cached entry only when it is not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244,
    27	# :283; a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, :600-620). Ant regenerates the AST
    28	# nodes, the parsers and Operators.java when an input is newer than the generated file (build.xml:371-384,
    29	# :450-467, :1335-1400); the checkout's own dates make it regenerate them, and javac then recompiles 1,077
    30	# files. And javac recompiles a source newer than its class (build-cache-exploration.md, section 6). So the
    31	# next `fortress compile` of a differing library source rebuilds it, and a worktree whose ProjectFortress/src
    32	# differs from B is seeded with a warning: the copied build is B's, so the worker runs ant compileAll, which
    33	# recompiles the differing sources (and deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356), and the library-order
    34	# recompile before its first compiled run. The base's own dates must be a build's: a base built in place by
    35	# ant, or seeded by this script.
    36	#
    37	# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
    38	# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
    39	#
    40	# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having
    41	# removed nothing, if the base is not built or not clean. Never touches the base or the main tree.
    42	# Run it from anywhere; it needs bash, git, python3, realpath and bc.
    43	set -euo pipefail
    44	
    45	BASE_ARG=${1:?usage: seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]}
    46	NEW_ARG=${2:?new worktree path}
    47	BRANCH=${3:?branch}
    48	BASE=$(realpath "$BASE_ARG")
    49	step () { local now; now=$(date +%s.%N); printf '%-34s %5.1f s\n' "$1" "$(echo "$now - $T" | bc)"; T=$now; }
    50	T=$(date +%s.%N); T_START=$T
    51	
    52	# The base must be built and clean, or its caches do not describe its commit.
    53	for f in ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/Shell.class \
    54	         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar \
    55	         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerLibrary.jar \
    56	         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/CompilerSystem.jar ; do
    57	    [ -e "$BASE/$f" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: $BASE is not built: $f is missing" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
    58	done
    59	if [ -n "$(git -C "$BASE" status --porcelain -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository)" ]; then
    60	    echo "seed-worktree: $BASE has changes under ProjectFortress, Library or default_repository:" >&2
    61	    git -C "$BASE" status --short -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository | head -5 >&2
    62	    exit 2
    63	fi
    64	B=$(git -C "$BASE" rev-parse HEAD)
    65	START=${4:-$B}
    66	
    67	# The worktree: the same command the batch workflow's shared prefix uses, with the base commit as default.
    68	if [ "$BRANCH" = - ]; then
    69	    [ -d "$NEW_ARG" ] || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q --detach "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
    70	else
    71	    git -C "$BASE" fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
    72	fi
    73	if [ ! -d "$NEW_ARG" ]; then
    74	    git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q "$NEW_ARG" "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null \
    75	      || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q -b "$BRANCH" "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
    76	fi
    77	NEW=$(realpath "$NEW_ARG")
    78	[ "$NEW" != "$BASE" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: the new worktree is the base" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
    79	if [ -d "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build" ] && [ -z "${SEED_FORCE:-}" ]; then
    80	    echo "seed-worktree: $NEW already has a build; left as it is (SEED_FORCE=1 replaces it)"

1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# old-fortress.sh <base-build> <private-caches> <fortress arguments>...
     3	#
     4	# Runs the old code, the base's: bin/fortress of the batch's one base build, with FORTRESS_HOME set to the
     5	# base build and FORTRESS_CACHES to a private caches folder. If the folder does not exist yet, it is first
     6	# made as a copy of the base build's default_repository/caches (36 MB, 0.04 s). The paths in those caches
     7	# are the base build's own, so nothing is translated, and no worktree is made.
     8	#
     9	#   old-fortress.sh <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss    the compiled path: compile ...
    10	#   old-fortress.sh <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches run P            ... then run
    11	#   old-fortress.sh <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss            walk
    12	#
    13	# Every cache a run writes goes to the private folder: every cache directory and the logs are under
    14	# fortress.caches (repository/ProjectProperties.java:283-299), which FORTRESS_CACHES sets, and
    15	# bin/fortress_classpath and bin/run_classpath put FORTRESS_CACHES/bytecode_cache on the class path.
    16	# Under the base build a run reads the build, the library sources and default_repository/configuration, and
    17	# writes nothing that stays: the parser writes its error logs beside each file it parses from source and
    18	# deletes them (compiler/Parser.java:349-367), so a compile of a program that exports Executable creates and
    19	# deletes two empty, gitignored logs beside Library/Executable.fsi. Two runs at once may share those two
    20	# names; that is harmless, because the base's library parses without errors, so both logs stay empty and
    21	# a log removed by the other run reads as empty (Parser.java:373-377). Measured in
    22	# explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md, section 6.
    23	#
    24	# Keep the private folder and your programs outside the base build (the program's own logs go beside it).
    25	# Refuses (exit 2) a base build that is not built, and a private folder inside the base build.
    26	set -euo pipefail
    27	USAGE='usage: old-fortress.sh <base-build> <private-caches> <fortress arguments>...'
    28	BASE=$(realpath "${1:?$USAGE}")
    29	PRIV_ARG=${2:?$USAGE}
    30	shift 2
    31	[ -x "$BASE/bin/fortress" ] && [ -e "$BASE/ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/Shell.class" ] \
    32	  && [ -e "$BASE/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar" ] \
    33	  || { echo "old-fortress: $BASE is not a built tree" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
    34	PRIV=$(realpath -m "$PRIV_ARG")
    35	case "$PRIV/" in "$BASE"/*) echo "old-fortress: $PRIV is inside the base build $BASE" >&2 ; exit 2 ;; esac
    36	if [ ! -d "$PRIV" ]; then
    37	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$PRIV")"
    38	    PART="$PRIV.part.$$"
    39	    cp -a "$BASE/default_repository/caches" "$PART"
    40	    mv -T "$PART" "$PRIV" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "$PART"     # another run made it first: use that one
    41	fi
    42	FORTRESS_HOME="$BASE" FORTRESS_CACHES="$PRIV" exec "$BASE/bin/fortress" "$@"
    43	#!/bin/bash
    44	# mg-run.sh <work-dir> <label> [threads]: the two microGPT checks under walk, each from an empty
    45	# private cache (FORTRESS_CACHES), each run from its own directory as its header says, both at once,
    46	# with bin/fortress's own JVM (JAVA_FLAGS -Xmx4g -Xss64m) and FORTRESS_THREADS=<threads> (default 1).
    47	# Output to <work-dir>/<name>.txt, headed by the machine line (machine.sh) and ended by rc=.
    48	set -u
    49	cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."                               # $FORTRESS_HOME
    50	export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH="/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH" FORTRESS_HOME="$(pwd)"
    51	unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
    52	export FORTRESS_THREADS=${3:-1}
    53	W=$(mkdir -p "${1:?usage}" && cd "$1" && pwd)
    54	L=${2:?usage}
    55	for f in explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlatCheck.fss explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptAplCheck.fss; do
    56	  (
    57	    t=$(basename "$f" .fss)
    58	    C="$W/caches-$t"; T="$W/tmp-$t"; rm -rf "$C" "$T"; mkdir -p "$C" "$T"
    59	    printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map"
    60	    {
    61	      bash explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/machine.sh "$L $t"
    62	      start=$(date +%s)
    63	      ( cd "$(dirname "$f")" && FORTRESS_CACHES="$C" JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$T" \
    64	          timeout -k 10 5400 "$FORTRESS_HOME/bin/fortress" "$(basename "$f")" < /dev/null )
    65	      echo "rc=$? secs=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))"
    66	    } > "$W/$t.txt" 2>&1
    67	  ) &
    68	done
    69	wait

# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.

OLD=${1:-}; NEW=${2:?usage: compare.sh <last-landed-table> <this-table>}
field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")

#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt"
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

## Shared prefix

Since 2026-09-30 the rung worker makes its own worktree, and the coordinator makes none at the launch (climb batch 7b's review, finding 9). In 7b no worktree was made at the launch, where the script's header said it launched "after the worktrees exist". W and S found none and made their own, and L's first run searched the tree for how. The header now says the worker makes it. "Your worktree" gives the one command, with the base, and the worktree and branch from the rung's tail: `git -C /home/user/fortress fetch -q origin BRANCH 2>/dev/null ; [ -d WORKTREE ] || git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add WORKTREE BRANCH 2>/dev/null || git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add -b BRANCH WORKTREE <base>`, then the push of the branch. The command reuses a worktree that exists after a VM restart and a branch already pushed after a container death, and otherwise cuts the branch from the base; its three cases were run on a scratch repository. Until 2026-10-02 `ant compileAll` and the library order then ran in each new worktree before its first build or test, since a plain copy of another tree's cache does not serve, its key hashing the source path; since then the command is `tools/seed-worktree.sh`, which makes the worktree with the same fallbacks and seeds it from the batch's base build with the path keys translated ("Climb batch 9", below). A symlinked build would still point every cache path at another tree (`batched-climb-review.md`, finding 2; FACTS, "The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box", for the two agents at once). The paragraph that said the build "has been copied in" says so, and the worker's retry is told to make the worktree if it does not exist.

New: a `run_bg`/`wait_for` pair at five-second granularity (item 7), whose bound is 270 s by default and, since 2026-10-02, at most, `wait_for` cutting a larger one to 270 (in climb batch 8 a bound of 280 let one wait run 289 s, past the prompt cache's life, and the next call wrote 464K tokens: `reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 6 and finding 5); a worker's scratch goes under its worktree's `tmp/<slug>/` and is never committed (post-mortem 2026-09-29); `ant` is never piped through `tail` (item i). Since 2026-09-29 the same section says that an agent stops or kills only processes under its own worktree's path, never by a script's name across the box: in climb batch 6.5b rung V stopped its own corpus pass with `ps -eo pid,args | grep -E 'count-run.sh|…' | … | xargs -r kill`, which also killed rung E's two base passes, run under a copy of the same runner, and E recorded their end as "the cause was not found" (`reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`, finding 4). Rule 2 asks for the site count when a precedent repaired a defect (item 6); rule 3 asks for the passage rather than the grep hit, ten lines either side (item 2). Rule 4's closing sentence, and the judge's `stop` question with it, named batch 3.5's two stops, a change to a declared type the prelude already has and a renamed or removed declaration a gated test uses, as if they applied to every batch; since 2026-09-26 both point to the stops the batch record's intro reserves for Pavol, at the head of the prefix (`open-items-2026-09-26.md`, item 27; batch 6's rung F changes declared types by Pavol's decisions). The register paragraph names a test by its topic and limits it to one comment line saying what it checks, with no pointer to a record (post-mortem 2026-09-29, section 2(c)). Since 2026-10-02 the re-anchoring rule for tests is gone (Pavol's yes of 2026-09-30; synthesis section 2(c)). Until then a rung that edited a specification chapter re-anchored, in its own commit, every `.tex` line its edit moved in the tests' messages and comments: batch 7b's rung S changed 49 test files and W 2, 310 lines in all. The one-time strip, `dc0eee2fe`, rewrote 823 specification citations in 139 test files to name the file and the section or entry. The rule in its place is in home 1's paragraph. A test cites the specification by its file and its section or entry by name, never by a line, and a new test does the same. A specification edit then moves no test's citation. What a citation is checked for is that the named section's text says what the message says: the skeptic's check 6. A rung that renames or removes a section a test names changes that citation in the commit of its edit, and that is the one test change a prose rung's skeptic allows (check 3). The rule stays in batch 7b's MANIFEST block, in its intro and rung S's tail, as 7b's record wrote it. The block is replaced whole at the next launch, so a record drafted for the next batch must not carry it. Since 2026-09-30 the paragraph after "Do NOT run ant testFast or ant testSystem" forbids a whole suite run any other way, except the one run per code state a checker or walk rung may make ("Preparing a batch record"), and the skeptic's closing paragraph has it read that run's result rather than run it again. "If your branch already carries commits" no longer tells a resumed worker to "re-run its checks rather than trusting its logs": a check whose log is complete stands unless the tree changed after it, and only a log cut off or failed is a step still to do. After 7b's VM restart, rung C's second run ran the compiler and library tracks and the distance stage again on a tree whose results were complete on disk, about 25 minutes of the box, because that sentence asked for it (`reviews/batch-7b-review.md`, finding 5). Since 2026-10-03 that section also names the predecessor's transcript (climb batch 9's review, finding 7): a run resumed after a restart starts the role again under the same key, so two lines, the run's directory found by the rung's worker labels and the journal's `started` lines listed with label, key and agent id, show the worker the restart stopped as the line before the worker's own with its key, its transcript `agent-<id>.jsonl` beside the journal, and the skeptic's two `jq` programs, moved above the prefix, read it. After climb batch 9's VM restart both resumed workers searched for it themselves, and W's search over every transcript ran past its 120 s timeout (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 5). And a paragraph after the whole-suite rule forbids a development run of a stage's driver on part of the library on the code the full stage then measures: the full stage runs once, when the code is final, with no partial run before it (finding 4). Rungs R and S of climb batch 9 did both on one code state, about 20 minutes of the machine, 18 of them on the critical path (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 2).

"Your briefing", added 2026-09-27 before the territory map, says what a briefing holds and who reads which part of it, and names no rung, so the prefix stays byte-identical across the batch's agents. Each role on a rung runs `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh` once, as its first step, with keys from the rung's manifest entry: the rung worker, and a worker resumed after a stop, read the whole `briefing`; the skeptic, the repair round after a refusal and the judge read its `checks` sub-list, and the judges on the merged tree read every rung's `checks`. The repair on the merged tree runs, since 2026-10-03, only the `checks` of the rungs its ruling's instructions name, by letter, slug or a path a rung's commit changed, and none where they name none (climb batch 9's review, finding 2): its review repair ran all four, about 85K bytes for W's alone, to fix one sentence about K's code, most of its 0.20M (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6). The rule is the same for the gate's repair, which shares the role. The tool prints each key's entry whole and in the order given: a `POSITIONS.md` entry by `positions:DATE WORDS` (the entry of that date whose head, its text up to the first colon and space, holds the words; from `POSITIONS-history.md`, saying so, when `POSITIONS.md` has none), a ledger row by `ledger:ROW`, a judge's ruling, a note's section or a specification section by `doc:PATH#HEADING` (in a `.tex` or `.tick` file the headings are its sectioning commands, macros dropped; a heading equal to the key wins over the ones that hold it, and `A > B` names B's section inside A's), a map section by `map:FILE#HEADING`, one table row, list item or bold-lead paragraph of a section by `@WORDS`, code by `code:PATH#FROM..TO` (from the declaration on the one line holding FROM through the end of the one at the next line holding TO, braces counted in Java and Scala, indentation and `end` in Fortress, with line numbers), a `FACTS.md` entry by its title and `INDEX.md` lines by `index:`. It prints in parts of at most 28 KB, under the 30,000 characters one shell command shows an agent, with `--part N` to continue, and opens with the size of the whole output in bytes and estimated tokens (0.41 a byte and 110 a part, the rate `explorations/reviews/worker-context-cost.md` fitted); `--check` prints where each key matches and its size, and `--root DIR` reads another checkout's record. The script refuses a key holding a double quote, a backtick, a dollar sign or a backslash, since each is rendered in double quotes, and a `checks` key missing from `briefing`. Until this change every such role also ran `--common`, the map README's three sections, `PLAN.md`'s phases and `repo-internals.md` whole, the same for every agent; no role runs it now. Pavol's reasons, 2026-09-27: the early climbs failed on agents' local decisions, and the record exists so that an agent works from the whole territory; and the briefing is in-context learning, since the agents were never trained on Fortress ("Preparing a batch record"). The reason for its shape is two reviews of that day: the misses of the later batches sat in ledger rows, `POSITIONS.md` entries, earlier judges' rulings and the library's own precedents, which neither `FACTS.md` nor the maps carry (`explorations/reviews/worker-global-decisions.md`); and a 29K-token read first, half of it `--common`, priced over the 78 agents measured, would have cost more than the gathering it could remove: on rung workers the cost fell inside the range it could save, and on skeptics and repairs it was a cost in every case (`explorations/reviews/worker-context-cost.md`).

"What a measured defect is worth" is the rule that closes the 22-and-2 gap. Every defect anyone measures has one of three homes and the record says which:

1. **repaired in the rung**, whoever measured it → an assertion in the rung's own gated test, passing before the second skeptic runs (item a);
2. **deferred, specification settles it** → a gated expected-failure test named `XXX…` asserting the specification's answer. The mechanism is cited so it can be checked: `FileTests.java:932` sets `shouldFail` from the name and `:587`/`:654` make `shouldFail != failed` the failure condition, so the suite goes red the day the test starts passing; `:851` names the case and the author's warning at `:853` is why a rung's first `XXX` file is shown to go red on a deliberate local fix (item b). Since 2026-09-29 the paragraph also carries the line that decides a run test, and two sentences with it (`reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`, finding 1 and measure 1). In `compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` an unmet `run_out_*` check fails a run test before the flag is read (`:534-539`, `:583-585`, before `:587`), and a run test with no such check demands `PASS` (`:276-282`); so an `XXX` run test's key names output the failing run does print before it dies, `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` where it dies before any output, never `run_out_contains=PASS`, citing the two `FACTS.md` entries on the mechanism. The first `XXX` file is shown through the harness itself, placed where the gate reads it and on the fix (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh` for `tests/`), not only by a direct compile and run. And a program the checker accepts that then fails JVM verification, linkage or a range check at run time is home 2, never 3 (`reviews/batch-N-review.md`, measure 6, which had not been built). The reason: climb batch 6.5b's rung V keyed its `XXX` run test on `PASS`, and it and its skeptic showed the red by a direct run, as the paragraph then allowed, citing exactly `:932`, `:587` and `:654`; only a briefing that carried the `FACTS.md` entry saw the rule, and in batch 7b one of four did. The gate went red on it, and the red cost 79 minutes and 1.2M tokens, a fifth of the run;
3. **deferred, specification silent** → a test pinning today's behaviour and a ledger row; where no program can observe it, the ledger row alone, quoting the output (post-mortem 2026-09-29).

A home-2 test is owed in the batch that measures the defect, even when a later rung or batch is planned to repair it; the argument that it can wait for the repairing rung was ruled against three times (batches 6b, 7R and 7C; `reviews/batch-7C-review.md`, the repeat; `reviews/process-review-6b-7-7R.md`, measure 3). The rule text the agents read carries the same sentence.

A report cites the Fortress tree and quotes its results; the tracked-path check is gone with the captures (post-mortem 2026-09-29).

"If your context is compacted", added 2026-09-29, tells every agent of the batch that its brief is the first message of its own transcript (the newest `agent-*.jsonl` under `~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/workflows/` whose first line holds the prefix's title and its role's heading), to re-read from it and from the files it wrote what its next step needs, and that the boot CLAUDE.md asks for after a compaction, the coordinator's `README.md`, the protocol, `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md`, is the coordinator's, as is the coordinator's session transcript. Batch N's gather ran that boot and searched the coordinator's transcript after its compaction, about 45K of its 70K tokens of re-orientation (`reviews/batch-N-review.md`, question 1; "Rules weighed by what they cost", below).

content.content:
## Climb batch 9: one base build, and a skeptic that reads (2026-10-02)

Pavol decided on 2026-10-02 that the skeptic checks that the test-first procedure was followed and does not repeat it, and that nothing is built or run twice on the same code (POSITIONS, "Test first, the test kept.", its last sentence, and "Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.": "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt."). He took four changes of the skeptic-scope judgement (`coordinator/skeptic-scope-judgement.md`, section 5, items 1 to 4) and the build and cache exploration's proposals (`coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`, section 5). The before is climb batch 8: 35 builds, 22 of them of a code state another agent had already built, about 85 minutes of the machine; a second whole gate after a repair of one sentence of the specification; the second skeptics' repeated list; about 0.5M written and an hour of the critical path in all (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 4; the exploration's section 4 puts the repeated work at 107 minutes and 230K tokens).

- **One base build, and every worktree seeded from it.** The coordinator builds one worktree at the base before the launch ("Before the launch", above), named by `args.baseBuild`. The prefix's "Your worktree" makes the rung's worktree with `tools/seed-worktree.sh <base build> WORKTREE BRANCH <base>`, which adds it with the same fallbacks as the old command and copies the base build's `ProjectFortress/build` and `default_repository/caches` with their path keys translated, in about 3 s, in place of `ant compileAll` and the library order in each worktree (the exploration, sections 1 and 3). If the seed exits 2, the worker makes the worktree and builds it itself, as before, and says so. "After an edit, and after a failed build" carries the exploration's rules for a worker (section 2): the edited component alone after a `.fss` edit, the five in order after an edit of a root api's `.fsi`, nothing under walk, `ant compileAll` with `global.map` restored and the library order before the next compiled run after Java or Scala, and never a wipe; the worker's step 5 and the merged-tree repair point to it. "The old code beside the new" gives the roles of a rung one private detached copy of the base, `<worktree>-base`, made by the first role that needs it with `seed-worktree.sh <base build> <worktree>-base - <base>` and reused by the rest, and runs in it with `FORTRESS_HOME` set on the command line, since `bin/fortress` takes `FORTRESS_HOME` from the shell whenever it is set (`bin/fortress_home`) and `env.sh` points it at the rung's worktree. A worker resumed after a crash sees its test fail there, not by reverting and rebuilding its worktree. Nobody compiles in the base build itself: every compile rewrites cache files of the tree it runs in, the foreign-Java `.tfi` and the `nativewrapper_cache` classes (the exploration, section 1), so two skeptics compiling there at once would write the same files, and the seed refuses a base that is no longer clean. A copy per rung, rather than the base build's `bin/fortress` with a private `FORTRESS_CACHES`, is the form the exploration measured as safe: no read of the base's path under `strace`. Each rung's roles run one after another, so no two agents ever compile into one copy. The commit stage removes the copies with the worktrees.
- **The skeptic builds nothing.** Check 3 reads test-first in the worker's transcript: the test committed alone before the fix, seen failing through the harness on the base's code in a run that ended before the edit was first built (under walk, before a library source it reads was edited), and seen passing in the worker's last run after its last change of code, with the lines `recordedFailure` and `recordedPass` quote. A test the transcript does not show failing on the base's code is refused, as one the skeptic could not see fail was before. "The worker's transcript" gives the two lines that find the transcripts (each agent's `agent-<id>.meta.json` holds its label, beside its `agent-<id>.jsonl`, in the run's directory) and two `jq` programs, one listing a transcript's edits, commits, builds and harness runs with their times and call ids (30 to 61 lines on batch 8's workers; on rung I's it shows the base run at 13:10, the test-only commit at 13:13:16 and the first build of the edit at 13:13:23), one printing a call's command and output. "You build nothing" says in one paragraph that the skeptic starts no build tool and no library compile, leaves the worktree on its commit, and compiles and runs only its own programs, with the rung's build for the new code and the rung's copy of the base for the old. A home-1 assertion (check 9) is read in the worker's passing run. A `testIsStage` rung's skeptic runs neither the count nor the distance stage: it checks in the transcript that the post-edit table was written on the head's code, and reads the distance table with `compare.sh`. The judgement's item 2 kept the 20-second count run as the test seen passing; POSITIONS' "no stage re-runs a build, a suite or a measurement on a code state another stage has already run" takes it too. The required differential keeps its purpose word for word, with one sentence on where its old side runs. `SKEPTIC_SCHEMA` gains a required `judgedHead`, the head the verdict judges, and `failureWasRecorded` now says what the transcript shows.
- **The second skeptic judges the repair** (the judgement's item 1). `secondSkepticRole` is its own brief: its first verdict as the script holds it, the judge's ruling, the repair round's structured result, the repair's commits and diff since the head the first verdict judged (its `judgedHead`; failing that, the parent of the commit that brought `SKEPTIC.md`), `SKEPTIC.md` and `JUDGE.md` left out, the repair round's transcript, and the one question whether the repair answers the refusal without breaking what the first judgement approved. It re-runs at the repaired head those of its own programs the refusal rests on and may write new ones for what the repair touches; nothing else of the first list. It writes its judgement at the top of `SKEPTIC.md` under "# Second judgement". In batch 8 a second skeptic cost about 350K, half of it the first list done again, and 15 to 20 minutes of each refused rung.
- **Three small fixes** (the judgement's items 2 to 4). No skeptic re-runs the distance stage (above). `skepticText` is the word `committed` once `SKEPTIC.md` is committed, and the text only when the harness refused the write, so that the skeptic no longer reads its file back and sends it a third time; the gather already prefers the file on the branch, and now deletes a journal-written file holding only that word and reports it missing. The skeptic's brief carries its rung's "For the skeptic" paragraph, taken from the tail word for word, with a sentence that the worker's recorded run stands where the paragraph asks for a build or a re-run; checks 6, 10 and 12 point to it, and the prefix's first paragraph says which part of the record each role's brief carries, where it said every brief carried the rung's section.
- **Four more, the same day** (`CLIMB-BATCH-9.md`, section 8, items 2, 4 and 6, and a gap this change opened). `STAGE_BLIND` names the test harness's sources ("Rules weighed by what they cost", item 5). The skeptic's check 8 is the review's check 3 ("Skeptic"). `wait_for` caps its bound at 270 s ("Shared prefix"). A second judgement whose write was refused beside a committed first one reaches `SKEPTIC.md` through a command of its own ("Gather").
- **The gate after a repair reruns only for a path it reads** ("A repair of tests and records only", below): under `ProjectFortress/` but a test file a passing run of the repair's exercised, under `Library/`, or `build.xml` (`gateReads`), for a repair's paths and the review's own corrections alike; a path no stage reads is recorded beside the gate's summary as `# repair-ungated`.

## The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage (2026-09-22)

The gate's eighth step runs the compiler's static checker over the **interpreter's** library and compares its error total with the last landed one. It answers Pavol's decision of 2026-09-21 (`POSITIONS.md`, "the library route"): one library, the interpreter's `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`, becomes the library the compiler checks, and the compiler's own prelude is deleted at the switch-over. Step 1 of `library-route-judgement.md` is what makes the distance a stage rather than a script — it was measured twice by hand (92 on 2026-09-16, 93 on 2026-09-19) and nothing kept it measured, which is the one-off validation these rules forbid everywhere else. Pavol's own objection is on record and this stage does not answer it: a count is a metric, not a measure of the work behind it (`postmortem-2026-09-19/positions-checker-gate.md`, 15:18).

The stage is `explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh`, with `WorldFlip.java` and the instrumented `StaticChecker` copy beside it — both copied from `perf-probes/prelude/`, so that the gate does not depend on a probe directory. It compiles the two against `bin/fortress_classpath`, puts the shadow checker ahead of `ProjectFortress/build`, and runs the compiler phase order over `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` with `Shell.useInterpreterLibraries()` under its own `-Dfortress.caches` in the gate's log directory: no library rebuild, nothing written into `default_repository/`, 20 s. Its table is one row per api with that api's error count, then `#total`, `#locations` (the distinct `file:line` the errors were reported at), `#crash` (the crash the checker meets after the apis — today the `nat` gap, `Not yet implemented` at `STypesUtil.scala:557`) and `#shadow`, which says whether the copy still matches the tracked checker, because a copy of a tracked source goes stale silently and then the number is not this tree's. `checker_compare` is red on a total that rose, on a changed crash line and on a stale shadow, each unless a rung of the batch declared it in `expectedCheckerCount` or `expectedCheckerCrash`; a total that fell is the batch's result and is reported, and the per-api rows and `#locations` are printed either way and are not themselves red. `last_landed_checker_count` finds the comparand the way `last_landed_summary` finds the summary, over `gate-baseline/checker-count.txt` and `climb-batch-*/gate/checker-count.txt`; the gate writes the table and commits nothing, and the commit stage lands it beside `summary.txt`, which is what keeps the chain of comparands unbroken. The first comparand is `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/checker-count.txt`, this change's own dry run on the tree at `6a6b36531`.

Until 2026-09-23 that comparison was a gate: a total above the last landed one was red unless it equalled a rung's `expectedCheckerCount`, and in climb batch 3 it went red on L's 103 against a declared 102. Since then the total is reported and is never red on its own, for the reasons in `checker-gate-review.md` (§ 2, and § 4, which recommends option (b) with (f)'s stale-copy check): a fix can raise the count, because the checker stops checking an api at its first errors (`StaticChecker.java:268-272`), and two rungs' changes do not add, so neither a rise nor a missed declaration tells progress from harm. `checker_compare` prints `COUNT UP`, `COUNT DOWN` or `COUNT SAME` with the last landed total, the measured one and the declared totals, as in `COUNT UP   93 -> 103, declared L: 102`, and exits 1 only on a crash line no rung declared, a stale shadow or a table with no total. Dry-run over the landed baseline and batch-3 tables, the rise exits 0 with or without a declaration, and a stale shadow or an undeclared crash change exits 1. `expectedCheckerCount` stays in the manifest as a prediction the gate prints. Explaining the change was the merged-diff review's job, its check 9 tying every new or risen row to a named rung edit, until the post-mortem of 2026-09-29 moved that check to the post-batch review, which reads the landed table and does not wait on the gate ("After the landing", below). The judge's `gate` question and the rung and skeptic briefs no longer say an undeclared rise is red. Two sentences still say the count may only fall and are left for their own edits: the header of `run.sh` and the manifest comment on `expectedCheckerCount`, which the next manifest replaces.

A rung whose manifest entry sets `testIsStage` has that stage as its test. The before is the last landed gate's table (POSITIONS 2026-09-28); step 3 of the order of work runs the stage once after the edit and its rebuild, to the worktree's `tmp/`, in place of the `.fss` component and its `.test` file; the skeptic's check 3 checks the report's diff against the two tables and, in the worker's transcript, that the run that wrote the post-edit one ran on the head's code (until 2026-10-02 it re-ran the stage itself; "Climb batch 9", below), and check 6 checks the two tables differ in the way the report says. Nothing else about such a rung changes — the ladder subset, the three homes and the provenance block all stand. This is the one place the test-first rule is met by a permanent stage instead of a test file, and the reason is that no program can yet be compiled against the interpreter's prelude (`library-route-judgement.md` § 2 step 1, which also sets the stop condition: two runs printing the same table). The first rung of the library route is the rung this flag exists for.

The overloading checker's memo is off in the stage since 2026-09-27 (`CLIMB-BATCH-7.md` section 8, item 2): `run.sh` passes `-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false`, read at `OverloadingChecker.scala:77`, and its table gains a `#cache` row before `#shadow`, which stays last. The memo is keyed on declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api reaches its overloading check (`perf-probes/nat/triage.md` section 1; `FACTS.md`, "The hidden layer, classified"). Until batch 7 the `FortressLibrary` api stopped before that check and the stage read the same either way; batch 7's rung H clears the api's early errors, and from then on a count taken with the memo on would depend on the build order. On the tree at `091b9b104` the stage reads 62 with the memo off and 62 with it on, the table otherwise byte-identical to the landed `climb-batch-6b/gate/checker-count.txt`, so the landed comparand stands and the first gate's diff shows the new row alone. The gate's step 8 says so and names the row.

## The distance stage (2026-09-27)

Pavol's answer 11 (`POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is driving it down". The count stage sees the errors before each api's early return, 62; with every stage of every unit run the checker reports about 1,740 (`FACTS.md`, "The true distance to the switch-over"). The stage is `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh`, the one-JVM run of `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat.md` section 5: `DistanceMulti.java` over the twelve prelude components, `FortressLibrary` first so that its run checks the twelve apis with every stage, under shadows that run every stage whatever the earlier ones reported and print each error (`add-patch.py`, on top of `desugar-codegen/shadow-patch.py`'s), the overloading memo off. The sources beside it are copies, as the count stage's are, so the gate does not depend on a probe directory: `DistanceMulti.java`, `shadow-patch.py`, `add-patch.py`, `errors.py` and the triage's `classify.py`, unchanged, their origin commits in the header; `table.py` is new and counts as `errors.py` and the triage's `fullerrs.py` count. The shadow classes are not copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each match once, so an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts, and the table's `#shadow` row then says STALE and it has no count. Nothing goes stale silently.

The setting is `any`, the compile path's pipeline with its extends-`Object` pre-desugaring off: the compiled path with the implicit bound `Any`. Answer 11 names the compile path's setting, and so does the record's section 1; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27, bounds an unbounded type parameter by `Any`, and the switch-over then takes that bound for the compiled path, so the 372 "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's and not the library's (`CLIMB-BATCH-7.md` section 1, Q1; `switch-over-distance-flat.md` sections 2.7 and 5, "under (a) the stage runs `stage-any`"). On the tree of 2026-09-27 `any` is walk's setting plus the compiled-expression desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions (class D1), one export error fewer and the variance checker's crash on `Stream`. The third argument of `run.sh`, `walk` or `compile`, runs another setting for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it. Rung B's classes N1, N2, R1 and R4 show under `any` as under walk's setting.

The table is tab-separated, one tagged row per fact: `#distance` (the setting and switches), `#total` (distinct errors), `#kind` (`errors.py`'s kinds), `#class` (the triage's root-cause classes, with their names), `#unit`, `#crash` (each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on), `#seconds`, `#machine` (the protocol's timing line) and `#shadow`, last. `errors.py`'s own count is checked against `#total`, and a `#check` row says so when they differ; its one-row-per-error list, `errors.tsv`, stays in the scratch directory for the sites. `compare.sh` prints DISTANCE DOWN, UP or SAME with the two totals, or DISTANCE FIRST, DISTANCE NO TABLE, SETTING CHANGED or SHADOW STALE where one applies, then each kind, class and unit whose count moved and each crash row that went or came, and always exits 0.

It is never red, on its own or otherwise. The record proposed red on an undeclared crash or a stale shadow, as `checker_compare` is (`CLIMB-BATCH-7.md` sections 6 and 8); this change follows the coordinator's brief instead, because the manifest has no field in which a rung could declare a distance crash, and a library edit moves one easily: `ExtentScalarRange`'s crash is hidden behind errors in its `case` clauses and returns once they check (`FACTS.md`, "The true distance to the switch-over"). A changed crash and a stale shadow are printed and reported in the gate's `distance` field.

Placement: step 2 starts the stage with `run_bg` right after `compileAll`, the one step whose output it reads, and step 9, after the checker count, waits for it with `wait_for` and appends `compare.sh`'s lines to `summary.txt`, each prefixed `# distance `. It is one JVM on one core with `-Xmx4g`, its own `-Dfortress.caches` and `java.io.tmpdir` under `tmp/gate-batch-<N>/distance/`, so the library rebuild, the suites (four tracks of `768m` each), the atomic runs and the ladder run beside it on the other three cores, and nothing they write is read by it. Run after them it would add 13 to 24 minutes to a gate of about 20 (batch 6's summary: `testFast` 5 min 50 s, `testSystem` 2 min 12 s); beside them it adds only what it outlasts them by. How much one taken core slows the suites and the atomic runs is not measured; the atomic runs' 120 s bound with one re-run stands. A gate retry finds the run by its `run_bg` log, which ends in `EXIT=` when the run is over, or by a java `DistanceMulti` running in the main tree, and never starts it twice (`recoverGate`). The commit stage lands `distance.txt` beside `summary.txt` and `checker-count.txt`, and `last_landed_distance` finds the comparand over `gate-baseline/distance.txt` and `climb-batch-*/gate/distance.txt`. None has landed, so batch 7's first gate prints DISTANCE FIRST unless the dry run below is landed first as `gate-baseline/distance.txt`.

A `testIsStage` rung starts the tool through `run_bg` right after its edit and reads it when its report is written, its before the last landed table and per-site list (the worker's step 3, since the post-mortem of 2026-09-29), and where its tail asks for the distance table its skeptic compares the worker's with `compare.sh` and re-runs nothing (check 3; until 2026-10-02 it re-ran the stage, 13 to 24 minutes, which skeptic M did in climb batch 8 for "DISTANCE SAME 545"). The count-table check, the merged-diff review's check 9 until then and the post-batch review's since, is not extended to this table, as the record's item 1 proposed: each rung's own tables against the landed ones already tie its moved classes to its edit.
